Day 1 · Internal planning topic

Welcome to Golden Bind

Introduce the library and invite the first browse.

Facts and context

  • Catalogue snapshot on 15 November: 1,107 public books; current count not rechecked.
  • Book Guides: people, places, maps and connections; coverage varies by book.
  • Writing workspace: free, private drafting, reader preview and chapter scheduling; writing requires an account.

Visual evidence / clip subjects

  • Approved Golden Bind logo/banner.
  • Current public catalogue capture, if used; refresh any count before release.
  • Optional book or page footage: obtain a source URL and verify the actual clip licence before selection.

Your writing

  • Owner/family writes introduction and personal reason for building Golden Bind.
  • Owner chooses the book-discovery question and link wording.
  • Owner writes all visible graphic text and accessibility description.

Format notes

  • One core introduction concept; adapt only after the owner supplies wording.
  • Short text, a still image or a short owner-recorded introduction are options; no requirement to use every format.

Sources to consult

  • Golden Bind public catalogue count Checked 2026-11-15

Day 2 · Internal planning topic

Maps beside the story

Show the distinctive Book Guide feature with one concrete book.

Facts and context

  • Great Expectations guide: illustrated map titled From the Marshes to London.
  • Map uses story proportions rather than survey distances; not a precise historical or navigation map.
  • Guide includes reading-progress controls; later-chapter pins and entries must stay out of early-reading captures.

Visual evidence / clip subjects

  • Actual public early-reading Great Expectations map capture.
  • Visible map/source/AI credits and a reviewed early-reading place card.
  • Frame-by-frame spoiler check; preserve the distinction between illustrated geography and surveyed locations.

Your writing

  • Owner explains what the map adds to their own reading.
  • Owner writes the qualification about story proportions in their own words.
  • Owner chooses the discussion prompt; script must reveal no later plot details.

Format notes

  • Map demonstration suits an image sequence or short screen recording with owner narration.
  • Use only the reviewed early-reading state in each platform version.

Sources to consult

  • Great Expectations Book Guide Checked 2026-11-15
  • Golden Bind Book Guides Checked 2026-11-15

Day 3 · Internal planning topic

Dickens and the weekly instalment

Connect literary history with today's serial readers and writers.

Facts and context

  • A Tale of Two Cities: 31 weekly instalments, 30 April–26 November 1859.
  • Smith College source also documents simultaneous illustrated monthly parts.
  • Instalments are not equivalent to chapters; no source claim that Dickens invented serial publication.

Visual evidence / clip subjects

  • Original calendar or instalment timeline graphics using owner-written labels.
  • Optional period newspaper, printing or book footage: candidate search only after sources and licences are checked.
  • Any archival scan or portrait requires its own rights record; factual citation does not clear an image.

Your writing

  • Owner writes the connection between serial publication and their own reading/writing habits.
  • Owner decides which verified dates and numbers are worth including.
  • Owner writes the source credit and any video narration.

Format notes

  • Research-led text, a timeline image or owner-narrated short video.
  • Keep the source reference available in the post description or accompanying research notes.

Sources to consult

  • Dickens Journals Online original weekly instalment index Checked 2026-11-15
  • Smith College rare-book exhibition Checked 2026-11-15

Copy, script, voice recording and release time: waiting for your input.

Day 4 · Internal planning topic

The challenge behind Frankenstein

Offer a memorable literary-history story without plot spoilers.

Facts and context

  • Frankenstein: conception and writing began in 1816; anonymous publication in 1818.
  • Mary Shelley: 18 when the story began, 20 at publication.
  • 1831 introduction: retrospective primary account of the ghost-story challenge.
  • Unsupported claims to avoid: completed in one night, competition winner, published at 18.

Visual evidence / clip subjects

  • Owner-created 1816/1818 timeline.
  • Optional lake, writing desk, manuscript or storm footage with individual licence checks.
  • No film-monster footage or historical image treated as reusable without evidence.

Your writing

  • Owner writes the story of the prompt and development period.
  • Owner chooses a personal observation or discussion question.
  • Owner writes chronology labels, source credit and narration.

Format notes

  • Owner-narrated short video or a simple timeline image.
  • Choose clips around the final human script; do not build a script around unverified stock footage.

Sources to consult

  • Shelley Godwin Archive Frankenstein chronology Checked 2026-11-15
  • Mary Shelley introduction to the 1831 edition Checked 2026-11-15

Copy, script, voice recording and release time: waiting for your input.

Day 5 · Internal planning topic

An invitation to writers

Make the original-fiction offer obvious and actionable.

Facts and context

  • Golden Bind writing page: free private workspace, reader preview and chapter scheduling.
  • Writing requires an account; reading a classic does not.
  • No evidence in this brief for audience size, author earnings or publishing outcomes.

Visual evidence / clip subjects

  • Approved brand graphics or owner-shot writing footage.
  • Optional real workspace demonstration with private drafts, account details and notifications excluded.
  • No fabricated published book, testimonial or author-result screenshot.

Your writing

  • Owner writes from their own experience of starting or maintaining a writing habit.
  • Owner explains the actual workflow they want to demonstrate.
  • Owner writes the invitation and account requirement accurately.

Format notes

  • Owner talking to camera, a brief real workflow demonstration or a text discussion.
  • Keep any demonstration separate from publishing real draft chapters.

Sources to consult

  • Golden Bind writing tools Checked 2026-11-15

Day 6 · Internal planning topic

Reading across languages

Introduce language discovery without promising universal translated editions.

Facts and context

  • Language shelves list published reading editions, including English, Urdu and Hindi.
  • Translated descriptions and translated chapters are separate; coverage varies.
  • A Tale of Two Cities edition example distinguishes source, AI/machine translation and description-only availability.

Visual evidence / clip subjects

  • Current language-shelf and edition-status captures.
  • Complete, partial and description-only states distinguished where shown; retain translation credits.
  • No translation request or paid generation triggered while capturing.

Your writing

  • Owner/family chooses which language experience to discuss.
  • Owner writes the distinction between edition availability and translated descriptions.
  • Human authors write each language version and verify edition-specific claims.

Format notes

  • Edition walkthrough, language-shelf stills or a human-written discussion post.
  • Review each language version separately; translation work is not part of this plan.

Sources to consult

  • Golden Bind language shelves Checked 2026-11-15
  • A Tale of Two Cities reading editions Checked 2026-11-15

Clips and timing

Choose footage after the script and shot list are agreed. For each candidate, record the original source, creator, license/permission, edit/commercial-use conditions and required credit. Downloadability alone is not clearance. No external clip has been sourced or cleared in this update.

Daily posting is the working cadence. Dates and clock times remain open until the first human-written posts and media are ready. Timing recommendations can use connected-account analytics; a new account's first slots are experiments, not a proven best time.
